'''Victor John Stenger''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|s|t|ɛ|ŋ|g|ər}}; January 29, 1935&nbsp;– August 25, 2014) was an American [[particle physicist]], [[philosopher]], author, and [[religious skepticism|religious skeptic]].

Following a career as a [[research scientist]] in the field of particle physics, Stenger was associated with [[New Atheism]] and he authored [[popular science]] books.<ref name= "Skeptic">{{cite web | url=https://www.skeptic.com/insight/the-fifth-horseman-the-insights-of-victor-stenger-1935-2014/ | last1=Shermer |first1=Michael |title=The Fifth Horseman: The Insights of Victor Stenger (1935–2014) | publisher= [[Skeptic (American magazine)]]|date=2014-09-20|access-date=2024-06-08}}</ref> He published twelve books for general audiences on [[physics]], [[quantum mechanics]], [[cosmology]], [[philosophy]], [[religion]], [[atheism]], and [[pseudoscience]], including the 2007 best-seller ''[[God: The Failed Hypothesis]]: How Science Shows That God Does Not Exist''. His final book was ''God and the Multiverse: Humanity's Expanding View of the Cosmos'' (2014). He was a regular featured science columnist for the [[Huffington Post]].<ref name=Skepticality_2012>[http://www.skepticality.com/les-folies-de-foi/ Audio of interview with Stenger on the podcast "Skepticality"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170706162108/https://www.skepticality.com/les-folies-de-foi/ |date=2017-07-06 }} released 28 August 2012 by the [[Skeptics Society]].</ref>

An advocate for removing the influence of religion from scientific research, commercial activity, and the political process,<ref>{{cite news|last=Stenger|first=Victor J.|title=The Fall of Foolish Faith|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/victor-stenger/the-fall-of-foolish-faith_b_1333412.html?ref=science|access-date=27 March 2014|newspaper=Huffington Post|date=9 March 2012}}</ref> Stenger coined the [[quotation|quote]]: "Science flies you to the moon. Religion flies you into buildings" (a reference to the [[September 11 attacks]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://old.richarddawkins.net/articles/3567 |title=Science flies you to the moon. Religion flies you into buildings. - Victor Stenger - RichardDawkins.net |publisher=Old.richarddawkins.net |date=2009-02-01 |access-date=2013-07-29}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Victor J. Stenger was born on January 29, 1935, and raised in a working-class neighborhood of [[Bayonne, New Jersey]]. His father was a [[Lithuanian people|Lithuanian]] immigrant, and his mother was the daughter of [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]] immigrants.<ref name="colorado.edu">{{cite web|url=http://www.colorado.edu/philosophy/vstenger/VWeb/Bio.html |title=A Biography of Victor J. Stenger |publisher=Colorado.edu |access-date=2013-07-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://ffrf.org/publications/day/victor-stenger | title=Victor Stenger | date=29 January 1980 }}</ref> He died on August 25, 2014, at the age of 79.<ref name=patheos20140830>{{cite web|url=http://www.patheos.com/blogs/friendlyatheist/2014/08/29/victor-stenger-physicist-and-prolific-atheist-author-is-dead-at-79/|last1=Mehta|first1=Hemant|title=Victor Stenger, Physicist and Prolific Atheist Author, is Dead at 79|website=Patheos|access-date=30 August 2014}}</ref>

==Career==

===Education and employment===
Stenger attended public schools in Bayonne, New Jersey, and received a [[Bachelor of Science]] in [[electrical engineering]] from Newark College of Engineering (later the [[New Jersey Institute of Technology]]). He then moved to [[Los Angeles]] on a [[Hughes Aircraft Company]] fellowship, earning a [[Master of Science]] and [[PhD]] in physics from [[UCLA]].<ref name="centerforinquiry1">{{cite web |url=http://www.centerforinquiry.net/oncampus/events/denver_victor_stenger_god_the_failed_hypothesis/ |title=[Denver&#93; Victor Stenger: "God: The Failed Hypothesis" |publisher=Center for Inquiry |access-date=2009-12-21 |archive-date=2015-09-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908123319/http://www.centerforinquiry.net/oncampus/events/denver_victor_stenger_god_the_failed_hypothesis/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was a member of the Department of Physics at the [[University of Hawaii]] until his 2000 retirement.<ref name="cv" /> He held visiting positions on the faculties of the [[University of Heidelberg]] in Germany and [[Oxford University]] (twice) and was a visiting researcher at [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.colorado.edu/philosophy/vstenger/Quantum/qmeta.html |title=Quantum Metaphysics |publisher=Colorado.edu |access-date=2009-12-21}}</ref> in [[England]], the [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare|National Nuclear Physics Laboratory]] in [[Frascati]], [[Italy]], and the [[University of Florence]] in Italy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pointofinquiry.org/victor_stenger_god_the_failed_hypothesis |title=Victor Stenger - God: The Failed Hypothesis |publisher=Point of Inquiry |date=2007-03-02 |access-date=2009-12-21}}</ref> He served as an [[adjunct professor]] of philosophy at the [[University of Colorado at Boulder]].<ref name="cv" /><ref name="origins">{{cite web|url=http://origins.skeptic.com/speakers_Stenger.php |title=ORIGINS — the BIG Questions: 2008 Skeptics Society Conference: Dr. Victor Stenger |publisher=Origins.skeptic.com |access-date=2009-12-21}}</ref>

===Scientist===
Stenger's first peer-reviewed work was published in 1964, and his research career continued until his retirement in 2000. His research involved work that determined the properties of [[gluons]], [[quarks]], [[Strangeness|strange]] particles, and [[neutrino]]s.<ref name="centerforinquiry1"/><ref name= "origins" /> Stenger focused on [[neutrino astronomy]] and very high-energy [[gamma rays]].<ref name="cv" /><ref name= "origins" />

===Philosopher and skeptic===
<!-- Cloned from net and reworded to avoid copyright issues. -->
Stenger was an advocate of [[naturalism (philosophy)|philosophical naturalism]], [[skepticism]], and [[atheism]], and wrote several books and papers about the [[relationship between science and religion]]. He was a prominent critic of [[intelligent design]] and the aggressive use of the [[anthropic principle]]. He maintained that if [[consciousness]] and [[free will]] do exist, they will eventually be explained in a scientific manner that invokes neither the [[mystical]] nor the [[supernatural]].<ref name= "Skeptic" /> He criticized those who invoke the [[interpretations of quantum mechanics|perplexities]] of [[quantum mechanics]] in support of the [[paranormal]], [[mysticism]], or [[supernatural phenomena]], writing several books and articles to [[debunker|debunk]] contemporary [[pseudoscience]].<ref name="VS@CSI">{{cite web |url=http://www.csicop.org/author/victorstenger |title=Victor Stenger |publisher=[[The Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]] |access-date=2009-12-21 |archive-date=2014-04-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140411005857/http://www.csicop.org/author/victorstenger |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Stenger took part in the 2008 "Origins Conference" hosted by the [[Skeptics Society]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]]<ref name= "origins" /> and debated [[Hugh Ross (astrophysicist)|Hugh Ross]] on the topic of whether science supports belief in [[existence of God]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=ORIGINS — The BIG Questions: 2008 Skeptics Society Conference | url=https://origins.skeptic.com/downloads/2008_Conference_Brochure.pdf | access-date=2024-12-15 | website=origins.skeptic.com}}</ref>

In 1992, [[Uri Geller]] sued Stenger and [[Prometheus Books]] for $4&nbsp;million, claiming [[defamation]] for questioning his "[[psychic]] powers." The suit was dismissed and Geller was ordered to pay [[court costs]].<ref name="Gellersuit">{{cite news | url=http://www.csicop.org/articles/uri_dis.html | title=Uri Geller Libel Suit Dismissed | publisher=[[Skeptical Inquirer]] | date=August 1994 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080211180550/http://csicop.org/articles/uri_dis.html | archive-date=2008-02-11 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Astronomer Luke Barnes argued in a 2012 paper that many of Stenger's claims about fine-tuning were problematic and that his arguments were fallacious.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Barnes|first1=Luke|title=The Fine-Tuning of the Universe for Intelligent Life|journal=Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia|date=June 2012|volume=29|issue=4|pages=529–564|doi=10.1071/AS12015|arxiv=1112.4647|bibcode=2012PASA...29..529B |s2cid=2951263 }}</ref> Stenger responded that Barnes misunderstood and misrepresented his positions.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last=Stenger |first=Victor J. |author-link=Victor J. Stenger |eprint=1202.4359 |title=Defending The Fallacy of Fine-Tuning |class=physics.pop-ph |date=28 Jan 2012 }}</ref>

==Professional and community positions==
* President, 1990–1994, Hawaiian Humanists
* Member of Editorial Board, ''[[Free Inquiry]]''
* Member of [[Society of Humanist Philosophers]]
* Fellow of the [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]]<ref>{{cite web|title=CSI Board, Fellows, and Staff|url=http://www.csicop.org/about/csi_fellows_and_staff/|access-date=16 July 2014}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[Center for Inquiry]]
* President, 2002–2006, Colorado Citizens for Science

===Columnist===
From 1998 to 2011 Stenger wrote for the column "[http://www.csicop.org/sb/archive/category/reality_check Reality Check]," in ''[http://www.csicop.org/sb Skeptical Briefs]'', the quarterly newsletter of the [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]] (CSI).<ref>{{cite web|title=Skeptical Briefs — Reality Check|date=2 June 2008 |url=http://www.csicop.org/sb/archive/category/reality_check|access-date=16 July 2014}}</ref>

Since August 2010, he was also a regularly featured science columnist for the [[Huffington Post]].<ref name=Skepticality_2012/><ref>{{cite web|title=Entries by Victor Stenger|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/victor-stenger/|publisher=Huffington Post|access-date=1 November 2014}}</ref>

==Pantheon of skeptics==
Stenger has been included in [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry|CSI]]'s Pantheon of Skeptics.  The Pantheon of Skeptics was created by CSI to remember the legacy of deceased fellows of CSI and their contributions to the cause of [[scientific skepticism]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Pantheon of Skeptics|url=http://www.csicop.org/about/the_pantheon_of_skeptics|website=CSI|publisher=[[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]]|access-date=30 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170131054129/http://www.csicop.org/about/the_pantheon_of_skeptics|archive-date=31 January 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>
